triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '12. TMA + warp-spec on small tiles with serial dependency = performance regression' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 12. TMA + warp-spec on small tiles with serial dependency = performance regression

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 12. TMA + warp-spec on small tiles with serial dependency = performance regression

payload.attempted: You replace cp.async with TMA for K/Q loads in the GDN chunk kernel, expecting TMA's hardware DMA engine to be faster. TMA is the "modern" approach on Blackwell and should outperform per-thread cp.async.
payload.lesson: TMA is NOT universally faster than cp.async. TMA wins when: - Tiles are large (≥64KB, ideally ≥128KB) - Double-buffering or multi-stage pipelining is possible - Producer work can overlap with consumer computation

established_fact.mechanism: 55% performance regression. P50 went from 1.1047ms (cp.async V1) to 1.7119ms (TMA V4). Correctness passes perfectly — purely a performance problem.

payload.observed: 55% performance regression. P50 went from 1.1047ms (cp.async V1) to 1.7119ms (TMA V4). Correctness passes perfectly — purely a performance problem.
